title: Proteins drift in a film of lipids under 5 nm thick, and sugars coat its outer face
subtitle: The plasma membrane as a fluid mosaic, drawn to molecular scale · a 34 × 20 nm patch, cut to show the bilayer
form: graphical abstract: pseudo-3D block, to scale
data: schematic; sizes after Nagle and Tristram-Nagle (2000)
alt: A graphical abstract: a 34 by 20 nanometre patch of cell membrane seen from above at an angle and cut open on two faces. The bilayer is 4.7 nm thick: two rows of phospholipid heads with fatty-acid tails between them and cholesterol rods tucked under the heads. A receptor of seven helices, cut open at the front, spans the bilayer, with a peripheral protein held under it on the inner side. A channel protein with a central pore and a glycoprotein rise from the outer face; short branched sugar chains sit on the glycoprotein and on glycolipids. A 5 nm scale bar.
note: Drawn in the Vellum 3D view with flat colour and one family per part. Heads 0.84 nm across and 0.82 nm apart, 3.9 nm between the head planes, helices 1 nm across, a channel 4.8 nm across; the receptor is cut so that four of its seven helices show in section.
